desc:
Legacy web app upgrade and modernization moves an older application to current tools in careful steps, so it keeps working while it improves. Ecom Swift LLC reviews your app, plans the safest route and tests every change against copies of your real data.

## What is a legacy web app upgrade?

A legacy web app upgrade is the process of bringing an older application onto supported frameworks, runtimes and databases without losing what it does. Some apps need a framework updated by a version or two. Others need a module rebuilt, a database moved or old libraries replaced.

The goal is not novelty. It is to make the app safe to run, quick to change and possible for a new developer to understand.

## Why does an outdated app become a risk?

Old frameworks stop receiving security fixes, and the libraries around them are abandoned one by one. Servers must stay on old software to run the app, which widens the gap each year. Few developers want to work in outdated code, so changes take longer and cost more, and the knowledge often sits with one person.

Performance suffers too. Pages written for earlier browsers and slower expectations feel heavy today. The longer an upgrade is delayed, the bigger and riskier it becomes, because the number of old pieces keeps growing.

## How an upgrade affects your results

A modernized app is cheaper to maintain, because developers can use current documentation and tools. It is safer, because security updates can be applied again. It is usually faster, and it is easier to extend with the features your users are asking for.

The business benefit is freedom. You are no longer held hostage by an old stack or a single person who understands it. The outcome depends on the starting condition of the app, which is why every project begins with an honest review rather than a promise.

## What a great upgrade includes

- A full review of the code, database, hosting and dependencies.
- A written upgrade route with a ranked list of risks.
- Small steps, each tested and released on its own.
- A copy of production data used to test migrations before anything goes live.
- Replacement of abandoned or insecure libraries.
- Database upgrades or tidying, with checks that records match before and after.
- Automated tests on key flows to prove old behavior is unchanged.
- A staging environment for your team to sign off each stage.
- A written rollback plan, rehearsed where the project is larger.
- Handover notes that explain the new structure for the next developer.

## What we do

We begin with a review and write down what the app does, what it depends on and where the dangers lie. Together we choose a route: upgrade in place, replace module by module or move to a new stack in stages. Each step is built, tested against your data copy and shown on staging before release.

The Basic package covers the review, an upgrade route and risk list, one safe framework or runtime step, testing of existing features and a rollback plan. Standard upgrades several modules, tidies the database, replaces old libraries and ends with a staging release for sign-off. Premium handles a larger move with data migration scripts and checks, automated tests, a before and after performance comparison, a cut-over plan, a rollback rehearsal and a handover call. Add-ons include extra modules, data clean-up and a documentation pack.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Share every piece you have, including old notes and server details.
- Tell us which features users rely on most.
- Take a full backup before each stage.
- Name one person who can approve staging.
- Keep a list of changes requested during the work, and add them after each stage.

**Avoid:**
- Attempting a complete rewrite in one jump.
- Skipping tests because the old app has always worked.
- Upgrading the database and the code on the same day.
- Deleting the old version before the new one has proven itself.
- Letting new features pile up in the old codebase while the upgrade is under way.

## Who it is for

This service suits a business whose original developer has left, an owner who has been told the framework is no longer supported, and a team whose app has become slow and fragile. It also suits companies that need a safe plan before a larger rebuild.

## What we need from you

Send the code or repository access, details of the hosting and database, and a description of what the app does and who uses it. We never ask for passwords. Access is granted as a collaborator or developer user, so you stay in control and can remove it at any time.
